title: Machine instruction admissibility
statement: For all natural numbers $C,e$, every Boolean value $m$, every finite bit string $h$, and every configuration $a$ consisting of an optional state, fourteen natural-number register values, and an optional Boolean result, the instruction specified at its active state satisfies its admissibility condition: a register-equality instruction compares distinct registers; an input-word comparison is used only when the input has the required plain or nested canonical encoding; and an oracle call uses a list of pairwise distinct argument registers.
hypotheses_covered: $a$ is a configuration with an optional state, fourteen natural-number register values, and an optional Boolean result
replaced:
For all natural numbers $C,e$, Boolean values $\mathrm{mode}$, every finite bit string
$h$, and every configuration $a$ of the specified fourteen-register machine, the
machine's instruction at the active state satisfies its precondition: any
register-equality test compares distinct registers, an input-word comparison is made
only on an input of the required plain or paired canonical form, and any oracle call
uses pairwise distinct argument registers.
